sentences.text: Tangvayosaurus is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous found in the Grès supérieurs Formation of Savannakhet Province, Laos.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial pelvis, several back vertebrae, a tail vertebra, ribs, and a humerus.
This animal reached a length of approximately 15 meters, a height of 6 meters, and an estimated weight of 15 tonnes.
The spinous processes of the posterior vertebrae are not bifurcated.
The ischium measures less than 90% of the length of the pubis.
Researchers suspected the phalanx formula was 2-3-3-2-1, though only nine phalanges have been found.
The type species Tangvayosaurus hoffeti was described in 1999 by a team led by Ronan Allain, and the species name honors French paleontologist Joshua Hoffet.
Allain et al. referred the old species "Titanosaurus" falloti, from the same geological formation consisting of a femur and tail vertebrae, to this genus as T. sp.
D'Emic (2012) found that Tangvayosaurus was the sister taxon of Phuwiangosaurus within the Euhelopodidae.
It lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 to 99 million years ago (Aptian to Albian), in what is now Asia.
The time range for Tangvayosaurus is the Aptian to Albian stages, from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago.
